deep.reconstruction:
This is p.5 of Grothendieck's preparatory notes for his Nov–Dec 1967 IHES lectures on crystals, which were published as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', notes by Coates–Jussila, in Dix exposés, 1968. The page continues a list of defects of classical algebraic de Rham cohomology, which motivates crystalline/infinitesimal cohomology.

Point (b), continued from p.4: singular varieties cannot be avoided. They appear, for instance, as fibres of morphisms of smooth schemes f: X → Y.

Grothendieck then poses the relative problem. For X smooth over C we already know H^*(X^an, C) ≅ H^*_DR(X) (his 1966 comparison theorem). One would therefore like a purely algebraic interpretation of the Leray spectral sequence of f^an: X^an → Y^an:
E_2^{pq} = H^p(Y^an, R^q f^an_* C) ⇒ H^{p+q}(X^an, C).

He remarks that even for f smooth this is not clear with the tools seen so far. He starts to write R^q f_*(Ω^•_{X/C}), crosses it out, and defers the matter to a later point.

In modern terms, the answer for smooth f is the following:
- the relative de Rham sheaves H^q_DR(X/Y) = R^q f_* Ω^•_{X/Y}, which are algebraic vector bundles;
- equipped with the Gauss–Manin connection, they form the algebraic counterpart of the local systems R^q f^an_* C;
- the Katz–Oda filtration of Ω^•_X by f^*Ω^i_Y ∧ Ω^•_X gives a spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p_DR(Y, H^q_DR(X/Y), ∇_GM) ⇒ H^{p+q}_DR(X).
- For non-smooth f one needs a crystalline or D-module framework.

He concludes with a programmatic requirement. A reasonable cohomological formalism should yield Leray spectral sequences 'as in the classical setting'. This is only possible if it admits coefficient 'sheaves' more general than de Rham complexes Ω^•_X. A marginal addition says these probably include complexes of differential operators more general than de Rham. In modern terms this is relative de Rham cohomology with coefficients in modules with integrable connection or crystals, or more generally D-module direct images and complexes of differential operators.

The page ends by opening point (c), duality, which is continued on p.6 with the call for an f^!, f_! formalism.
errors: No mathematical errors. The Leray spectral sequence is written correctly with E_2 converging to H^*(X^an, C). The remark that even smooth f poses difficulties is historically accurate for 1967: the Gauss–Manin connection was only being made algebraic by Katz–Oda (1968).

ideas.what: Request for a purely algebraic (de Rham) interpretation of the Leray spectral sequence of a smooth morphism of complex varieties
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection and Katz–Oda (Leray) spectral sequence in algebraic de Rham cohomology
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968), introduction and the Gauss–Manin discussion; also suggested to Katz–Oda

ideas.what: Leray spectral sequences require coefficients more general than the de Rham complex, including 'complexes of differential operators more general than De Rham'
ideas.modern_name: Crystals / modules with integrable connection as coefficients; D-module direct images; differential complexes (Herrera–Lieberman, M. Saito)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968) introduction; Récoltes et Semailles (discussion of de Rham coefficients / crystals of differential operators)

ideas.what: Singular varieties are unavoidable even when studying smooth ones, because fibres of morphisms of smooth schemes may be singular (motivating infinitesimal/crystalline cohomology)
ideas.modern_name: Infinitesimal site / Hartshorne's algebraic de Rham cohomology of singular varieties
ideas.where_published: On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties (Publ. IHES 29, 1966); Crystals (Dix exposés 1968)

deep.surprise_reason: These are preparatory lecture notes whose motivational content (the defects of de Rham cohomology: char p, singular varieties, the Leray spectral sequence, duality) appears essentially verbatim in the published introduction to 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'. The hint toward general complexes of differential operators as coefficients anticipates D-modules, but Grothendieck himself publicly claims this anticipation in Récoltes et Semailles, so it is not new to the record.
transcription_corrections: Line 'En fait, [-même-] si f est lisse': the struck word is a short scribble (possibly '='), not clearly 'même'.

'Nous y reviendrons au point 4[?] : l'heure[?]' is uncertain. The written words over the crossed-out formula and on the next line read roughly 'Nous y reviendrons ... à point ... l'heure'; the reading 'point 4' is doubtful, and the phrase may be a 'later / in due course' type expression.
The crossed-out formula is R^q f_*(Ω^•_{X/C}) with a bracket, crossed out together with the following line '... des faisceaux définis sur Y, par des'.

'Une formulation cohomologique vraiment raisonnable devrait indiquer': the verb may be 'impliquer'. 'l'écriture de suites spectrales' may read 'l'existence de suites spectrales'; the image is ambiguous, and 'impliquer ... l'existence' fits the sense better.
'vraiment' is the struck-out word, with 'cohomologiques' written above it as a replacement.
